text: Kobak et al. build a counterfactual baseline by linear extrapolation from earlier years (q = p_{Y-2} + 2*max{p_{Y-2}-p_{Y-3},0}) and deliberately exclude 2023 because it may already be LLM-affected. (medium confidence)
keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection

text: Control by word class: authors hand-annotated 900 excess words from 2013-2024 as content (about 51%) or style (about 45%); Covid-era excess was mostly content nouns, 2024 excess mostly style verbs and adjectives, which separates topical drift from LLM tics. (low confidence)
keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection

text: Excess-word counts are only a lower bound on LLM use, and cannot distinguish LLM use from authors independently adopting LLM-preferred vocabulary. (low confidence)
keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection

text: Excess words are flagged using two metrics, frequency gap and frequency ratio; thresholds were chosen so most pre-Covid years fall well below them, giving conservative estimates. (low confidence)
keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection

text: Human baselines for model-output tic detection can be built from pre-2022 corpora (wordfreq for single words; Reddit creative writing and Project Gutenberg for n-grams in Antislop), with overuse expressed as a ratio of model frequency to baseline frequency. (medium confidence)
keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection

text: Post-2021 web text is contaminated by generative-AI output, so frequency resources built from it no longer measure human language; wordfreq's maintainer stopped updating it for this reason, forcing baselines to pre-2022 archives. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2024-09-15)
keywords: Human baselines and control words for tic detection
